Our 3E model: Emit, Echo, Evolve

The waves in Figure 1 bring different perspectives into the same conversation. Our 3E model describes how we work with those perspectives: make a question understandable, listen to the response, then use it to reconsider what we do. We return to the conversation when a change raises a new question.

Emit — make the question clear
We explain what ORCA is trying to do, what remains uncertain and why we are asking for input. The question after our banana-DNA activity showed us that explaining an experiment also means discussing its connection to everyday life.
Echo — listen for what we missed
We ask what matters to the person responding. Clinical conversations raised treatment burden; research discussions challenged specificity and function; care-center feedback drew attention to readable materials and limited staff time. Each perspective adds a different part of the problem.
Evolve — make a considered response
We connect feedback to an action and a record: revise the workbook, give delivery burden greater attention, or stop a partnership when resources and responsibilities do not align. The chapters below distinguish changes we made from questions that still need follow-up.
